newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:
* Senate Republicans have proposed a offered up a package of tax cuts that the Clinton administration said slightly improves upon the House Republican version that was passed last week.
* On the 25th anniversary of the Watergate break-in, some of the chief characters involved in the political drama have been resurrected and others have found ways to make money off the scandal.

* All eyes are on Pensacola, Fla., the first place where time limits for receiving welfare expire. While it hasn't proved to necessarily be the motivator that pushes recipients to get jobs, it also hasn't pushed recipients into deprivation.
* The suspect in the 1993 fatal shooting outside the CIA's headquarters in Virginia has been seized in Afghanistan.
* The suspect in a bombing that killed 19 Americans in Saudi Arabia last year has been deported to the United States.
* Gunfire erupted in Cambodia's capital, the result of fighting between forces of two feuding prime ministers.
* Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver is an understated and shy politician, a rarity in New York, yet he ended up playing a central role in resolving the conflict over the state's rent laws.
